title: Carriage No. 13
subtitle: One carriage, two carriages ... Don't look too closely at the thirteenth.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: *muffled* Mmff. Get off me!

items.speaker: Deep Voice
items.text: Alright, she's down! Bring the garlic, stake, and salt!
Heavy hands cover her face, coal smoke, garlic, and earth choking her breath until she nearly faints.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ugh! What're you ... *chomp*

items.speaker: Urgent Voice
items.text: Careful, Yakov! Don't let her bite you!
Finally, the grip loosens. She scrambles to her feet.
The Extra Carriage
Her eyes adjust to the dark.
No vampires, no bats, no endless corridors, just an ordinary, if grim, old carriage.
Dozens of filthy "passengers" crowd together, ragged and tense, clutching makeshift weapons: iron rods, pans, even garlic and salt.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: Wait, it's just a kid. You're not a vampire, are you, young lady?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Course I am! You're looking at the heir of Dracula the Impaler himself!
They raise their "weapons" once more.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa! Let's not be too hasty. This vampire's already got a full belly.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: For now.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: Then tell us why you broke in here. And don't go telling lies.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I …
Rubuska tries to step back, but the cold iron door blocks her retreat.

items.speaker: Stowaway Passenger
items.text: Cut her some slack, Yakov. I don't think she meant any harm.
A woman's voice calls out, gentle but firm.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: Hmph. Reyhan, every time we try to act tough, you go soft on us.

items.speaker: Reyhan
items.text: Maybe so, but what other option do we have? If anyone hears us and comes looking, we're done for.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Sh-She's right. Let me go, and I won't say a word. I-I didn't see a thing, promise.
Ugh ... *cough*
A child whimpers in her arms, and Rubuska hesitates.
The woman hugs him closer, soothing him.

items.speaker: Reyhan
items.text: It's alright, Ivanushka. No need to be afraid. We've got our eyes on her.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: I'm not afraid. She isn't half as scary as those whizz-bangs.
The boy leans against the woman, one sleeve hanging empty.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: How much longer will we be stuck here, Rey? Will we really go to Budapest?
Reyhan lowers her head, stroking his hair softly.

items.speaker: Reyhan
items.text: Of course we will, little guy.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Budapest? Then, you're also …
No words are needed. The scene says it all.
That scent, too familiar. The nightmare returns, always chasing her ...

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: Kolyo *sniffle* Kolyo, don't fall asleep, okay?
Gunfire still echoes. A village burns behind her. She clutches her brother, unable to look back at the ruins.

items.speaker: Kolyo
items.text: Buska, I can't feel my legs.

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: They're just a bit numb. It'll pass. You'll be fine. *sniff* I'll get us out of here.
Flames tear across the sky. A shell bursts overhead.

items.speaker: Kolyo
items.text: I think my legs are gone.

items.speaker: Kolyo
items.text: It-It hurts, Buska. It-It hurts so bad. I can't—

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: Oh. You'll be fine, Kolyo, alright? Your big sister's here. You're safe.

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: You'll feel better tomorrow. You'll be better.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: Um, Ms. Vampire, what happened to your eyes? They've gone all red and watery, like a white rabbit's.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Huh? Oh, it's nothing. Happens every time I think of a happy memory. It's a vampire thing.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Hm?
She hears a faint sound by the door.
Step by step, quiet and patient.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: What is it?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Shh!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Someone's coming.
Rubuska signals the others to hush then presses her ear to the door.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Strange, I don't hear anything now. Was it just my imagination?
She lowers her head and sees a dim yellow glow seeping through the crack.
A shadow blocks the light, swaying with the train.
She turns in panic but meets the gaze of a helpless boy.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: Are the bad men coming for us again?

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: I don't want to go with them.
His blue eyes look almost clear in the darkness.
Once before, in a world of ash and gunfire, another boy had looked at her the same way.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Kolyo …
She draws a deep breath, making a solemn vow.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: … You're not going anywhere. I swear it on my honor as a vampire.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Just leave it to me. I'll get you all to Budapest, safe and sound.
Turning back, she faces the door.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Now, keep quiet.
They hold their breath.
Dozens of eyes weave a net around her, holding her spine steady, sealing every path of retreat.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Whoever you are …
She spreads her arms, coat flaring wide, like a bat unfurling its wings in the night.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Sh-Show yourself! But don't think I'll let you touch a hair on their heads!
An effortless battle, yet the defeated refuses to yield.
Oh! That's quite enough!
I'm warning you—no fangs on the train, Rubuska.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Huh? What are you doing here?
Hearing her name called in that familiar voice, the girl slackens her grip.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Funny, I had intended to ask you the same thing.
The yellow beam falls across weary, half-wild faces.
No one speaks. Her speed and skill intimidating the onlookers.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No sign of Squad 77, and these people don't look like Manus, either. Could they be the "cargo" she was talking about?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Are they civilians?
She pauses for a moment, then speaks again.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Who brought you on board? The conductress? Think before you answer. I know more than you think.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Why are you on this train?
Silence. Eyes filled with unease and suspicion fix on her. She knows only sincerity will break through the wall between them.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Just listen please, I don't work for the border patrol, the army, nor the railway.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: If it's war, famine, or death you're running from, well, who could blame you? In times like these, anyone would do the same.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: My business here is with a vampire. If you don't have anything to do with one, then your purpose here is of no concern to me.

items.speaker: Stowaways
items.text: A vampire?
All at once, they turn to Rubuska.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Could she mean me? Did you come here looking for me?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I can see what you're all thinking, but it's not her. I thought perhaps it could be hiding in this carriage, but it appears I was wrong.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Oh ...
She nods, unsure whether in relief or regret.

items.speaker: Stowaway I
items.text: So the stories are true. Good thing we came prepared!

items.speaker: Stowaway II
items.text: That vampire … It won't find us, will it?
Worried murmurs ripple through the carriage.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Look, I'm willing to help you, but only if you give me some information about yourselves. After all, trust is a two-way street, right?

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: I understand.
Yakov surveys the faces, sighing under his breath.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: We're refugees; we come from all over. Someone offered us a way out, and we took it. It's nothing more than that.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: We were told to wait near Belgrade station until a train stopped.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: They said someone would attach this carriage to the rear, and as long as we kept our heads down and stayed quiet, we could make it across the border.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: As for the conductress ... She didn't speak much. She said there'd be people on the other side, people who'd feed us, give us medicine, help us start a new life in Budapest.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: That's the whole of it.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She's taking a huge risk for you. Smuggling you across the border could put her behind bars. She asked for a fair price, I assume?
The passengers shake their heads.

items.speaker: Reyhan
items.text: No, nothing. Only that we keep quiet and never speak a word about it to anyone who doesn't need to know.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Whoa ... I never would've figured her for something like that.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But that Manus insignia ... How did she get it? And why did she give it to those soldiers?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And I can't forget that the rest of my squad has vanished without a trace.
Semmelweis takes a glance outside—an unyielding screen of white snow.
She checks her watch.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: We'll be reaching the checkpoint any minute now.
Their time is short.
As if to confirm her calculation, the train begins to slow.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: We're stopping again. What's going on?
Yakov presses close to the door, peeking through the crack. His eyes suddenly brighten.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: You're right. It's the border checkpoint!

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: Good news, folks—by tomorrow, we'll be out of the country!
